## Disposition: credited prior counterexample and source repair

For 30006513 / OWR-14299587-002, the literal catalogue formulation over arbitrary omega-categorical structures and oligomorphic sets is false by a verified published binary counterexample. The original OWR finite-length question assumes a countable structure homogeneous in a finite relational language and W=M^k for a positive integer k. That original restricted question is NOT resolved. The separate general ascending-chain question is not disproved by a descending chain.

Credit Mikołaj Bojańczyk, Joanna Fijalkow, Bartek Klin, and Joshua Moerman, TheoretiCS 3 (2024), Article 13, Theorem 4.16, Lemmas 4.14–4.15 and Appendix B. Zero new substantive proof-search turns; no novelty claim. This releases the binary prior-proof-availability hold and proposes an explicit formulation repair. No QUEUE change.

Read the complete, byte-preserved accepted/SOURCE_SCOPE_AND_PRIOR_PROOF_AUDIT.md and accepted/SOURCE_SCOPE_REPAIR.md. For V=direct_sum_N F_2 and G=GL(V), the incidence-sum modules C_n have minimum nonzero support 2^n and form strict infinite descent. Deleting the zero coordinate on C_1 gives the projective chain, with minimum support 2^n-1. Exact faithful scalar extension preserves strictness over every characteristic-2 coefficient field. The bounded-arity circuit argument explains why the same GL(V) action has no homogeneous finite relational presentation. The infinite conclusion rests on the written mathematical arguments and induction, not finite tests.

No all-characteristics negative claim, odd-characteristic failure, general-finite-base-field extrapolation or resolution of the original OWR question is asserted. The same vector-atom action has finite length in characteristic zero by the stated LICS scope. Definition 5.1/Theorem 5.4 retain their bounded finite-approximation hypotheses. Theorem 7.3 and Corollary 7.5 retain their unary/binary free-amalgamation restrictions, with only stated Corollary 7.8 consequences. Positive theorem statements and organization were inspected, not every proof certified; the final conference paper defers some second-method technical details to a full version.

Evans arXiv:2603.29606v2 (9 September 2026) is distinguished from v1. LICS final Article 82 is distinguished from the provisional author Article 6. Earlier Evans–Gray and Ahlbrandt–Ziegler proof bodies were not retrieved; no first-priority or broader historical theorem certification is made.

Public sources:
- OWR source: https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/52445 ; https://doi.org/10.4171/OWR/2025/58
- Evans v1: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.29606v1 ; latest inspected v2: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.29606v2
- Complete directly audited prior counterexample: https://doi.org/10.46298/theoretics.24.13 ; https://www.cs.ox.ac.uk/people/bartek.klin/papers/theoretics24.pdf
- Final positive-theorem source: https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.LICS.2026.82

## Verification boundaries and exact evidence

All seven accepted files remain byte-identical. The retained accepted/verify_known_chain.py is historical: it uses assertions removed by optimization and writes CHECK_RESULTS.json adjacent to itself. Its execution is explicitly NOT_RUN. We do not claim the entire packet's code is assertion-free. The separate current_checks.py neither imports nor executes the historical checker; it uses independently operative explicit guards, writes no output file, and recomputes finite cases under normal/-O/-OO.

Per optimization mode, fresh checks verify seven accepted document identities and two exact scope declarations, ten finite (d,n) cases with 1<=n<=d<=4, 317 GL-generator incidence checks, 60 containment checks, 60 hyperplane identities, 125 ternary-relation triples, and the dependency obstruction. Eight substantive finite-algebra source mutants are rejected for exact intended reasons, retaining their complete raw stdout/stderr. These counts corroborate small finite algebra only, not the infinite proof or positive theorem proofs.

Separately, per mode: 41 integrity rejections, 64 schema/scope rejections, 46 complete-output comparator rejections, and 27 physical create/append-open/unlink denials pass at actual UID=EUID=1000. Full raw mode-specific stdout/stderr and recursive exact JSON types/values/identities/counts are checked. Empty, malformed, changed, skipped, expected-failure, altered identity/count and wrong-mode outputs are rejected for fixed reasons. Hostile current-directory/Python-environment imports match the complete clean baseline, and before/after hashes show all delivery bytes unchanged.

CHECK_RUNS.json and raw references are pre-seal reference-capture receipts bound by the manifest; final sealed replay receipts remain outside its inventory. Historical checker/result execution, source-body, historical retrieval/inspection, excluded-material, new-source search, dataset, full positive-theorem proof, earlier historical counterexample proof, formal proof-assistant and infinite-theorem computational-certification replays are NOT_RUN. Public source hashes and retrieval/inspection history record the accepted earlier audit, not fresh publication-stage network provenance verification. Only authored audit/source repair, acceptance, safe current checks, preserved historical check evidence and public source metadata are included. No source bodies, datasets, private sources, private personal/coordination material or identifying metadata for excluded private material are delivered.

## Public reproduction and noncircular trust chain

Repository packet: unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30006513

Authenticate BOOTSTRAP.py with the fixed SHA-256 below from this independently reviewed description before executing it, then copy that authenticated file outside the packet. Do not derive the trust anchor afresh from the download under verification. Set all packet files to 0444 and directories to 0555; run as actual UID=EUID=1000:

- python -I -S -B /trusted/BOOTSTRAP.py --controls /path/to/packet
- python -I -S -B -O /trusted/BOOTSTRAP.py --controls /path/to/packet
- python -I -S -B -OO /trusted/BOOTSTRAP.py --controls /path/to/packet

The fixed external bootstrap binds the verifier, manifest and mutation harness. The manifest binds every other delivery byte, including historical files, code, declarations, receipts and raw references. It excludes only itself and BOOTSTRAP.py, whose hashes are bound outward. Final receipts stay outside this inventory to avoid circular hashes and are pinned below. The runtime and standard library are trusted; file modes protect against accidental writes, not root or deliberate owner chmod.

The exact additive diff was applied in a fresh relocated directory, then all three positive replays were required to reproduce the complete sealed baseline stdout/stderr byte-for-byte. All 24 files were unchanged. No source theorem is computationally certified.
